title: Minimax-Regret Precision Allocation across Two Experimental Sites for Lipschitz-Coupled Policy Targets

tldr: For two experimental endpoints and several Lipschitz-coupled policy targets, does allocating endpoint precision in proportion to the welfare weight of targets nearest each endpoint solve the entire minimax game? The proposal investigates an exact affirmative theorem in the clustered regime \(2D\le r\), uniformly over known \(C\), common variance \(v\), fractional budget \(N\), arbitrary measurable vector treatment rules, and nature-before-realization randomized allocations. Matching antipodal Bayes and mixed-sign certificates would establish the value \(F(Cr,\sqrt{v/N})\) and the exact transition from a sign decision to a probit treatment probability.
gap: Public theorem text solves the scalar bounded-bias treatment problem and related separable enrollment problems, but does not determine endogenous two-endpoint shares for several policy targets coupled by one Lipschitz effect function and unrestricted vector decisions. The closest-looking 2026 Liu manuscript could not be inspected, so collision risk remains open rather than being resolved from its abstract.
